messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p95 latency alert for hosted-east-1/generation (route: /v1/generate). p50 95ms -> 140ms, p95 210ms -> 980ms over last 12m. Multiple customers seeing errors. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:
jen: acked, i'm oncall. i'm looking at dashboards now. which teams should i pull in?
kumar: infra-oncall here. i'm seeing node-level CPU scheduling stalls on the GPU fleet. runqueue lengths jumped on several hosts ~6m ago.
lia: devex — customer reports: interactive chat sessions lagging, some timed out at 30s. small fraction but a few enterprise sessions impacted.
ryan: i'm with tracing — getting spans now, looks like tail latency correlates with long kernel context switch waits and higher syscall latencies. attaching a sample trace id: trace: 0x7fb1c3
sam: marking impact: partial degradation for hosted customers in east region, not global. notifying support for affected tenants.
jen: quick mitigation options? can we failover traffic to hosted-west or fall back to smaller model variants?
kumar: we can shift 20% of routed traffic to west via routing policy in 3-4m, but will increase latency for those requests. fallback to smaller models is doable per-route.
lia: let's initiate soft fallback for non-low-latency SLAs: route generation requests to quantized-variant-v2 if latency > 400ms. Ops, can you push that rule?
ops-bot: @jen submitted routing change request id 3456. Will apply after 30s testing window.
jen: applying now. also spinning up 10 extra inference pods in east pool to absorb queue.
ryan: past 10 traces show kernel scheduling wait spikes. here's a short perf snippet from a problematic host (abridged):
```
# perf record -a -g -- sleep 5
# perf top sample
10.2% [kernel] schedule
8.4% [kernel] do_syscall_64
6.1% [user] inference_worker
4.5% [kernel] __switch_to
```
jen: that schedule/do_syscall pattern screams kernel-level stall. any recent node-level OS/kernel changes?
kumar: yes — we pushed a minor kernel upgrade (6.4.12 -> 6.4.15) in the maintenance window ~20m before spike to a subset of nodes (10% canary then promoted). rolling back is an option but will be disruptive.
lia: is there a known bug in 6.4.15 around scheduling?
ryan: i searched upstream — there was a recent patch that changed RCU/kthread wakeup behavior. also see increased context switch counts in perf counters: ctx_switches up 5x.
sam: immediate ask: can infra isolate a few hosts that show the worst runqueue length and remove them from LB? remove will drain pods.
kumar: isolating three worst hosts now: ip-10-0-5-12, ip-10-0-6-22, ip-10-0-7-03. taking them out of rotation.
ops-bot: draining pods on ip-10-0-5-12 (pod ids: r-infer-3a, r-infer-7b).
jen: good. once drained, observe p95 for 1m. also keep the routing fallback in place.
ryan: tracing update after drains + routing change: p95 improved from 980ms -> 420ms. still above baseline but much better. p50 back to ~120ms.
lia: customer impact update: support notified, we sent heads-up to impacted tenants, PS team standing by.
jen: hypothesis list (in-thread):
- H1: kernel 6.4.15 scheduling change + workload pattern caused runqueue growth under certain GPU-intensive syscalls.
- H2: a coincident user traffic pattern (larger batch sizes) increased KV cache thrash leading to syscall bursts.
- H3: networking driver (a NIC firmware bump) increased syscall blocking, appearing like scheduler stalls.
jen: we need data to prioritize. ryan, please collect perf counters + ftrace from affected hosts. kumar, capture `vmstat 1 60` and `dmesg` from those hosts. lia, confirm exact customer sessions/timestamps.
ryan: starting ftrace capture with `trace-cmd record -e sched_switch -e sys_enter -e sys_exit -o /tmp/trace.dat 60`. will upload when done.
kumar: `vmstat` samples (aggregated) show:
```
procs -----------memory---------- ---swap-- -----io---- -system-- ------cpu-----
 r  b   swpd   free   buff  cache   si   so    bi    bo   in   cs us sy id wa st
 4  0      0 1024M  512M 5120M    0    0   120    48  5600 32000 40 12  5 43 0
```
kumar: cs (context switches) ~32k/s during spike window.
lia: logs from service show retries and timeouts around 23:11:05 UTC. I'll add matching user timestamps to the timeline.
jen: recording timeline in doc: 22:50 maintenance window kernel canary -> 23:10 canary promoted -> 23:20 p50/p95 shift begins -> 23:22 alert -> 23:24 rollback started? (we haven't rolled back).
sam: decision time: do we roll kernel back for promoted nodes or continue with draining + routing until a full patch is validated? Rollback risky if not identical images.
kumar: rollback plan: replace kernel package with previous image and reboot — takes ~6m/host. We can target the remaining promoted hosts and bath them out.
ryan: additional trace insight: long spans surface inside `sys_enter_ioctl` and near GPU driver ioctl code. that points to driver/kernel interaction, not purely scheduling.
lia: given driver involvement, vendor firmware/driver might be root cause — need vendor engineering loop. Opening a ticket.
jen: immediate mitigation stance: keep routing fallback + drained hosts; continue scaling to cover capacity. Don't rollback promoted hosts immediately; plan targeted rollback for worst-cases if p95 doesn't reach <250ms in 30m.
sam: i've handed this to next oncall (sam-night) at 00:10 UTC with notes: drains in effect, routing fallback active, traces collected, action: if p95 > 350ms after 30m, execute rollback on remaining promoted hosts.
ops-bot: @sam-night: oncall handoff recorded. Incident severity: Sev2. Postmortem owners: jen, kumar, ryan.
jen: thanks — continuing to monitor. i'll post upload links for traces and perf archives in 10m. everyone, if you find anything new drop it here. :thumbsup:
ryan: uploaded trace bundle: https://files.internal/reports/trace-2923456789.tar.gz (contains ftrace + perf + flamegraphs).
kumar: uploaded `dmesg` and vmstat logs to the same bundle.
lia: sent customer follow-ups. preparing RCA outline for post-incident.
jen: closing live mitigation loop for now — leaving thread open for RCA coordination.
